body.p: AMENDMENTS TO THE CLAIMS The following listing of claims replaces all previous listings and versions of claims in this application.

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) A method of adjusting analyte sensor data, comprising:
storing, by processing circuitry, at least one parameter including a slope associated with a sensitivity of an analyte sensor;
collecting, by the processing circuity, sensor data with from an-the analyte sensor when at least partially inserted into a human bodyinterstitial fluid of a user, the sensor data including data indicative of a level of an analyte in the interstitial fluid;
obtaining, by the processing circuity, a shelf duration of the analyte sensor;
adjusting, with by the processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to compensate for at least a first duration of time, wherein the first duration of time is one of athe shelf duration, or a wear durationthe adjusting comprising adjusting the slope associated with the sensitivity of the analyte sensor; and
determining, by the processing circuitry, the level of the analyte of the user from the sensor data using the adjusted slope; and
outputting an analytethe determined level- of the analyte to a displayrepresentative of the adjusted sensor data.
2. (Cancelled)
3. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the first duration of time is the shelf duration, the method further comprising determining the shelf duration with the processing circuitry.
4. (Original) The method of claim 3, wherein the shelf duration is representative of a period of 2 time after the analyte sensor was manufactured and before the analyte sensor was inserted into the human body.
5. (Original) The method of claim 3, wherein the shelf duration includes the entire time the analyte sensor was in a packaged state prior to insertion into the human body.
6. (Original) The method of claim 5, wherein a wait period is implemented such that the shelf duration is representative of a time period less than the entire time the analyte sensor was in a packaged state prior to insertion.
7. (Original) The method of claim 3, wherein the adjusted sensor data is different from the collected sensor data.
8.(Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the analyte sensor has a the sensitivity at least partially represented by a slope and/orthe one or more parameters further comprises an intercept, and wherein adjusting, with by processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration further comprises adjusting at least one of the slope and the intercept.
9. (Cancelled)
10. (Original) The method of claim 3, further comprising collecting temperature data representative of a plurality of temperatures to which the analyte sensor was subjected during the shelf duration.
11. (Original) The method of claim 10, further comprising adjusting, with processing circuitry, the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration and the plurality of temperatures.
12. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the first duration of time is the wear duration, the method further comprising determining the a wear duration with processing 3 circuitry, and adjusting, by the processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to compensate for the wear duration.
13. (Original) The method of claim 12, wherein the wear duration is representative of a period of time during which the analyte sensor is at least partially inserted into the human body.
14. (Original) The method of claim 12, wherein the wear duration begins upon insertion of the analyte sensor into the human body.
15. (Original) The method of claim 12, wherein a wait period is implemented such that the wear duration begins a period of time period after insertion of the analyte sensor into the human body.
16. (Original) The method of claim 12, wherein a sensor control device comprises the analyte sensor and sensor electronics, and wherein the wear duration begins upon activation of the sensor control device.

23. (Original) The method of claim 3, wherein adjusting, with processing circuitry, the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration comprises:
adjusting, with processing circuitry, the sensor data with a function comprising an adjustment parameter and a value representative of time.
24. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the adjustment parameter corresponds to a code selected from one of a plurality of codes, the method further comprising:
decoding, with processing circuitry, the code to determine the adjustment parameter.
25. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the adjustment parameter corresponds to a code selected from one of a plurality of codes, the method further comprising:
communicating the code from a sensor control device to a reader device;

decoding, with processing circuitry of the reader device, the code to determine the adjustment parameter; and
adjusting, with processing circuitry of the reader device, the sensor data with the function comprising the adjustment parameter and the value representative of time.
26. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the value representative of time is representative of a shelf duration.
27. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the value representative of time is representative of a shelf duration less a wait period.
28. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the adjustment factor is stored in memory in an unencoded form, the method further comprising:
adjusting, with processing circuitry, the sensor data without decoding the adjustment factor.
